rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: True creation includes complete estimation and separation: God alone encompasses every limit and can restore what creatures cannot reassemble, as successive prenatal creation illustrates.
rows.anchor: فلا يملك الخلق والفرق إلا من يملك الجميع والرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling creatures creators is a potentially misleading appearance: all creation, including acts in the visible and unseen realms, belongs to God. This grounds tawhid and the community's faith; al-Qadariyya are called this community's Magi.
rows.anchor: وتلايح تحت هذا اللبس في إطلاق اسم الخالق على الخالق الحق ذي الحول والقوة والقدرة والإحاطة

rows.speaker: شاعرهم
rows.claim: The cited poet distinguishes making something from completing it: some people create or estimate, then fail to carry the work through; the line witnesses تفري.
rows.anchor: كما قال شاعرهم : ولأنت تفري ما خلقت وبعض القوم يخلق ثم لا يفري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Bāriʾ refines, separates, and repairs what was estimated so it can receive its form; full knowledge yields exact preparation, while limited makers leave defects that may thwart the intended result.
rows.anchor: { البارئ } أي الذي يدقق بما وقع به التقدير ويقطعه ويصلحه لقبول الصورة على أتم حال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Muṣawwir completes visible detail, plan, and bodily parts; beyond outward form comes only the subtle maturation of an enlivened creature toward its appointed perfection.
rows.anchor: التصوير إتمام تفصيل الخلق الظاهر وإكمال تخطيطه وإحكام أعضائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A building illustrates the names' stages: an engineer estimates the plan, craftsmen prepare stone and timber, and builders assemble the form; only God fashions with full wisdom and perfection.
rows.anchor: ويتضح الفرق جدا بين الأسماء الثلاثة بالبناء فإنه يحتاج أولا إلى مقدر يقدر ما لا بد منه

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī says fashioning reaches every part of the world, even an atom, an ant, and each ant's organs; its intricate structure and wisdom point to its fashioner.
rows.anchor: قال الرازي في اللوامع : والتصير موجود في كل أجزاء العالم وإن صغر حتى في الذرة والنملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The beautiful names belong exclusively to God, including the wisdom necessary for fashioning; human beings cannot apprehend Him fully.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى : { له } أي خاصة لا لغيره { الأسماء الحسنى } اي من الحكيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imperfect verb signals that God's creatures continually renew their glorification, a reminder to deficient beings of His abiding perfection.
rows.anchor: دل على دوام اتصافه بذلك من يحتاج لما له من النقص من الخلق إلى التذكير فعبر بالمضارع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The construction with لَهُ conveys exclusive glorification of God through the object restriction and the preposition lā m.
rows.anchor: على وجه التخصيص بما أفهمه قصر المتعدي وتعديته باللام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He omits ما before الأرض and joins it directly to heaven, hinting that earth shares heaven's elevation as evidence of God's perfection, like one entity.
rows.anchor: كالشيء الواحدج بإسقاط ( ما ) وألصقها بها إلاحة إلى ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿAzīz is the One who overcomes everything, has no equal, is difficult to reach, and is urgently needed.
rows.anchor: العزيز } أي الذي يغلب كل شيء ولا يغلبه شيء ولا يوجد له مثل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wisdom is perfected judgment brought to a firm conclusion that cannot be overturned.
rows.anchor: من الحكمة وهي إتقان الحكم وإنهاؤها إلى جد لا يمكن نقضه

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī defines judgment as restraining and directing someone for their good: it appears forceful but is inwardly gentle, disliked at first yet yielding later satisfaction and relief.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : المنع عما يترامى إليه المحكوم إيالة عليه وحمله على ما يمتنع منه نظرا له

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī illustrates bodily judgment as medical treatment, citing the instruction to seek treatment and that God sent a remedy with illness; no grading or source is stated.
rows.anchor: فموقعه في الأبدان المداواة ( تداووا عباد الله فإن الذي أنزل الداء أنزل الدواء )

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī applies judgment in religion to obeying rulings, patient striving, and confronting outward enemies and inward enemies such as the self, family, and Satan.
rows.anchor: وموقعه ف الأديان التزام الأحكام والصبر والمصابرة على مجاهدة الأعمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sura's aim is to explain Friday's gathering: it is a central Islamic obligation requiring attendance, disengagement from other affairs, and unity around the purifier in worship and struggle, hardship and ease.
rows.anchor: مقصودها بيان مسمى الصف بدليل هو أوضح شرائع الدين وأوثق عرى الإسلام وهو الجمعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the basmala, God's knowledge encompasses every known thing and completes its explanation.
rows.anchor: { بسم الله } الذي أحاط علمه بكل معلوم فتم بيانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Raḥmān's mercy extends the blessing of explanation after the generosity of bringing creation into being.
rows.anchor: { الرحمن } الذي عمت نعمة بيانه بعد شمول كرامة إيجاده فهو العظيم شأنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Raḥīm grants His party success in what pleases Him, establishing love and faith in their innermost hearts.
rows.anchor: { الرحيم } الذي خص حزبه بالتوفيق لما يرضاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The previous sura's account of some Israelites turning away, and God turning their hearts, establishes His complete power and the knowledge and transcendence that follow from it.
rows.anchor: ولما ختمت الصف بالإقبال ببعض بني إسرائيل على جنابه الأقدس بعد زاغوا فأزاغ الله قلوبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Three preceding suras asserted glorification in the past tense at their openings; this sura uses the imperfect to affirm its renewal and continuity alongside God's enduring dominion.
rows.anchor: ذكر التسبيح الذي هو الأعظم الأشهر للتنزيه بلفظ الماضي ثلاثة مرات في افتتاح ثلاثة سور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb means to enact the greatest, most splendid, and most perfect glorification.
rows.anchor: أي يوقع التنزيه الأعظم الأبهى الأكمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording reinforces God's sovereignty as in al-Taghābun; once the occurrence of universal glorification is acknowledged, further emphasis is unnecessary.
rows.anchor: وأكد بذلك لما في التغابن ولم يحتج بعد الإقرار بالوقوع على هذا الوجه إلى التأكيد بأكثر من مرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rational creatures glorify either willingly in obedience or unwillingly through submission to God's will, while inanimate things glorify willingly in every state.
rows.anchor: تسبيح الصامت طوعا في كل حال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He repeats the conjunction for what is on earth because the address to believers calls for further emphasis.
rows.anchor: دعا ذلك إلى التأكيد لاحتياجهم إليه فقال : { وما في الأرض } كذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding three suras establish that all beings glorified God; this sura says glorification continues anew, and together with transcendence this proves His complete perfection.
rows.anchor: وأخبرت هذه باستمرار ذلك على سبيل التجديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Malik possesses every perfection and can aid His army, even when weak, until it prevails.
rows.anchor: { الملك } أي الذي ثبتت له جميع الكمالات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Quddūs is free of every defect; nothing happens without His permission, and creatures cannot encompass His knowledge or grasp His essence, only witness His acts and reflect on His attributes.
rows.anchor: القدوس } الذي انتفت عنه جميع النقائص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person most worthy of nearness is one who models God's attributes as far as effort allows; believers should avoid saying what they do not do and acting without sound judgment.
rows.anchor: المتخلق بأوصافه على قدر اجتهاده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿAzīz overcomes all and cannot be overcome; He could make rational creatures glorify Him willingly as well as submit to His will unwillingly.
rows.anchor: { العزيز } أي الذي يغلب كل شيء لا يغلبه شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ḥakīm places everything He wills in its wisest, most complete, and most exact setting.
rows.anchor: الحكيم * } الذي يوقع كل ما أراده في أحكم مواضعه

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr links the sura to al-Ṣaff's close, which praised the disciples for their response and faith and commanded believers to imitate them.
rows.anchor: وقال الإمام أبو جعفر بن الزبير : لما ختمت سورة الصف بالثناء على الحواريين

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr says the call to imitate Jesus's disciples could imply that they outrank Muhammad's followers, so the sura follows by praising Muhammad's community.
rows.anchor: كان ذلك مما يوهم فضل أتباع عيسى عليه السلام على أتبع محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم فاتبع ذلك بذكر هذه الأمة

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: He reads the opening glorification as clearing the doctrinal implication of the unbelieving faction mentioned at the end of al-Ṣaff, whom he says made a grave claim about prophethood.
rows.anchor: فافتتحت السورة بالتنزيه عما أشار إليه قوله

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: The passage praising the Messenger and his community answers the possible impression that Jesus's followers possess greater virtue.
rows.anchor: هو الذي بعث في الأميين رسولا منهم

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: The parable of people who carried the Torah but failed to bear it warns the newly praised community not to repeat their failure.
rows.anchor: مثل الذي حملوا التوراة ثم لم يحملوها كمثل الحمار يحمل أسفارا

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr explains that the Torah-bearers' fate warns those praised earlier not to become like them: they were hated and cursed after failing to uphold the Torah; the warning is merciful, and only the discerning reflect.
rows.anchor: وهي في معرض التنبيه لمن تقدم الثناء عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Purifying rude, resistant people by making them affirm transcendence demonstrates God's power; having said Israelites refused purification and strayed, the author infers His power to purify all rational beings.
rows.anchor: ولما كانت القدرة على تزكية الجلف الجافي بحمله على التنزيه أدل على القدرة على غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: هُوَ means God alone; بعث describes sending from the hidden presence with the law's commands and prohibitions.
rows.anchor: أي وحده { الذي بعث } أي من حضرة غيب غيبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ummiyyūn first means the Arabs, known among other peoples for not writing and remaining in the original, natural state of birth.
rows.anchor: أي العرب لأنهم كانوا معروفين من بين سائر الأمم لا يكتبون بل هم على الخلقة الأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He also allows the word to include all Earth's people: knowledge had disappeared when the Prophet was sent, and Arabs are the root while other peoples follow them.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن تطلق الأمية على جميع أهل الأرض لأن بعثه صلى الله عليه وسلم كان حين ذهب العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Messenger's being from the same people makes their reform through one of their own kind remarkable; his unlettered state is an abiding natural quality, without learned artifice, while his knowledge came without acquisition.
rows.anchor: ولما كان تقويم الشيء بمثله أعجب قال : { منهم } بل الأمة بمعنى عدم الكتابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although his mission began among the Arabs, his origin does not restrict his mission: explicit texts and decisive proofs establish that he was sent to all humanity.
rows.anchor: وذكر بعثه منهم إن خص الوصف بالعرب لا ينفي بعثه إلى غيرهم ولا سيما مع ما ورد فيه من الصرائح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يَتْلُوا means to recite one passage after another, repeatedly and with elevation.
rows.anchor: { يتلوا } أي يقرأ قراءة يتبع بعضها بعضا على وجه الكثرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His recitation is a clear proof of his truth: though unlettered like his audience, he brings verses while many among them can write and learn, a gift only the omnipotent could grant.
rows.anchor: مع كونه أميا مثلهم { آياته } أي يأتيهم بها على سبيل التجدد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tazkiya removes base morals and deviant beliefs. In this context it precedes instruction because some had fallen into affection for disbelievers; during the Prophet's life, his loving gaze, teaching, and recitation purified people.
rows.anchor: { ويزكيهم } أي عن الأخلاق الرذيلة والعقائد الزائغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī recounts that Umayr ibn Wahb, after plotting with Ṣafwān to kill the Prophet following Badr, was guided by him; after Mecca's conquest Umayr brought the fleeing Ṣafwān back, who then converted, and Umayr became a leading Companion.
rows.anchor: فأما عمير فكان من أعظم المؤذين للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ولمن آمن به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's call gave al-Ṭufayl ibn ʿĀmir al-Dawsī a light as a sign; he called his family and people, and none of his people held back from Islam.
rows.anchor: وكذا ذو النور الطفيل بن عامر الدوسي رضي الله عنه ثم قومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For people beyond the Companions, the Prophet's traces purify according to their receptivity and God's preparation; stronger longing brings firmer adherence to Qur'an and Sunna and deeper knowledge and practice.
rows.anchor: وأما غير الصحابة رضي الله عنهم فتزكيته لهم بآثاره بحسب القابليات والأمور التي قضى الله أن يكون مهيأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Book is the revelation sent to the Prophet, gathering every kind of religious and worldly good in this life and the next.
rows.anchor: ويعلمهم الكتاب } اي المنزل عليه الجامع لكل خير ديني ودنيوي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wisdom is the Book's goal: understanding joined to practice, and practice mastered by transmitted and rational knowledge, so each matter is placed well and they avoid Israel's deviation; this teaching alone would suffice as a miracle.
rows.anchor: وهي غاية الكتاب في قوة فهمه والعمل به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because unlettered status can imply misguidance, and many thought themselves on a sound religion, وإن emphasizes that they truly were in misguidance before the Prophet, despite the possibility of later straying again.
rows.anchor: وكان كثير منهم حال إنزال هذه السورة يعتقد أنهم على دين متين وحال جليل مبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before the Messenger came, the Arabs had abandoned the religion of their forefather Ismāʿīl and worshipped idols; their misguidance was plain.
rows.anchor: { من قبل } أي قبل إرساله إليهم من حين غيروا دين أبيهم إسماعيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their misguidance appeared in obvious false beliefs, widespread ignorance willingly embraced, and scorn for those who sought learning and insight, as with Zayd ibn ʿAmr ibn Nufayl.
rows.anchor: باعتقادهم الأباطيل الظاهرة وظنهم أنهم على شيء وعموم الجهل لهم ورضاهم به واختيارهم له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This description rules out human instruction of the Prophet, magnifies his inimitable revelation, and shows how urgently they needed a messenger to guide and rescue them.
rows.anchor: فوصفهم بهذا غاية في نفي التعلم من مخلوق عن نبيهم إعظاما لما جاء به من الإعجاز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The others are non-Arabs who share the unlettered condition, not Arabness; God will bring even foreign commoners into the Arabs' knowledge and purification.
rows.anchor: { وآخرين } أي وبعثه في آخرين

rows.speaker: ابن عمر وسعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUmar and Saʿīd ibn Jubayr identify the others as non-Arabs who will join the Arabs; this is also transmitted by Layth from Mujāhid, and the author says the report supports his reading.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما وسعيد بن جبير أيضا رضي الله عنه

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abū Hurayra reports that when a man asked who the others were, the Prophet placed his hand on Salmān and said that if faith were at the Pleiades, men from his people would reach it; no grading is given.
rows.anchor: ما روي عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه أن رجلا سأل عنهم لما نزلت سورة الجمعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's might lets Him purify and teach anyone, even the dullest people; His wisdom makes what He wills conform to His law in an exact, unbreakable form and ensures its execution.
rows.anchor: فهو يزكي من يشاء ويعلمه ما أراد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ذَٰلِكَ points to God's great elevation of the Messenger and his people, making the once-marginal Arabs leaders; favor is an unowed gift, bestowed on whomever He prepares by His power.
rows.anchor: { ذلك } أي الأمر العظيم الرتبة من تفضيل الرسول وقومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is the possessor of all perfection, and His immense favor makes every gift from others seem small.
rows.anchor: { العظيم * } أي الذي يحقر دونه كل عطاء من غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After describing resurrection's effect on life, the passage turns to inanimate things and starts with the lower world, closely connected to people and therefore more instructive to them.
rows.anchor: أتبعه التأثير في الجمادات , وبدأ بالسفليات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By divine power the earth is shaken and spread out, while the mountains are lifted, pulverized into scattered dust, and left without any stone or mound.
rows.anchor: { وحملت } أي بمجرد القدرة { الأرض } أي المنبسطة ورجت رجا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountains are treated as one mass to intensify the crushing: earth and mountains are flattened and pounded together until no part is distinguishable.
rows.anchor: { فدكتا } أي مسحت الجملتان الأرض وأوتادها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dakka is a level expanse, like a camel without a hump or level land; the author says dakk and daqq are related, with dakk more forceful.
rows.anchor: من قولهم : ناقة دكاء , أي لا سنام لها

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān distinguishes the terms: dakk scatters the particles, while daqq mixes them together.
rows.anchor: قال أبو حيان : والدك فيه تفرق الأجزاء , والدق فيه اختلاط الأجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يومئذ is repeated after a long separation, stands as a substitute from إذ, and heightens awe; the time phrase is governed by وقعت.
rows.anchor: فيومئذ } أي إذا دكتا وهي بدل من ( إذ ) كرر لطول الفصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The event is the promised and threatened Resurrection, imagined as a massive weight that must fall; its several names heighten awe, and the intended event is the second blast.
rows.anchor: فكانت كأنها شيء ثقيل جدا ليس له ممسك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the lower world, the account turns to the upper world: the sky as a whole splits from the day's severity and becomes weak, falling, light, and unable to hold together.
rows.anchor: ذكر العلوي فقال : { وانشقت السماء } أي هذا الجنس لشدة ذلك اليوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-malak is a broad category applying to one or more; its placement on the sky's edges means its sides, rims, and borders of what has not split.
rows.anchor: والملك } أي هذا النوع الذي يصدق على الواحد فما فوقه , والجمع لا يصدق على ما دون الجمع
